dedupe_keys.name: agencia nacional de mineria anm colombia mining cadastre web feature service

description: This web feature service publishes the geographic layers of Colombia's mining cadastre maintained by the Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM), the national mining authority. The service lists 14 layers: current mining titles (Titulo_Vigente), current applications, subcontracts, applications for and declared special reserve areas, restricted indigenous areas, ethnic mining zones, strategic mining areas, state investment areas, areas susceptible to mining, reserved zones with potential, an area bank and regional service points. It is produced by the ANM, whose SIGM mining management system also exposes the same data. Coverage is national for Colombia. The layers can be read free by any GIS or client supporting OGC WFS and saved as shapefiles or as attribute tables in CSV or XLSX; a third-party guide by geoactivismo.org, updated in July 2026, shows how to do this in QGIS. Caveats: the service metadata leave fees and access constraints blank and no licence was found, the layer names are in Spanish with no field documentation on the pages read, and titles change as applications are granted. For simulation it shows where mining titles and restricted areas lie relative to rivers, roads and communities, for hazard exposure and land use conflict studies. It is related to the Sernageomin and Spanish mining cadastre records in this catalogue.
